title: Per-player chat rate limiting in a game gateway
name: Game chat rate limiter

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code rate limits players? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In RateLimit, why does the per-player check run before the shared server budget check?
choices: A rejected player request does not consume a token from the shared server budget, so one noisy player cannot drain capacity for everyone else
It makes the Retry-After header more accurate because the player bucket refills faster than the server bucket
The server limiter is not safe for concurrent use, so it must only be reached by one request at a time
Authenticate would otherwise overwrite the limiter state for the player

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of RunSweeper, and what is the cost of sweeping a bucket for a player who then returns?
choices: It flushes pending reservations to the server limiter; a returning player loses their queued requests
It bounds the size of the buckets map by deleting idle players; a returning player gets a fresh full bucket, which is harmless once the idle time exceeds the refill time
It resets all buckets each minute so that limits are aligned to wall-clock windows
It keeps the Authenticate session cache warm so that returning players avoid re-verification

questions.prompt: Under heavy concurrent traffic from many players, which statement about the limiter map and its lock is accurate?
choices: Because Go maps are safe for concurrent reads, the lock is only needed in Sweep
A second request for the same new player can create a duplicate bucket because the lookup and the insert are not atomic
The mutex serializes every token-bucket decision, so throughput is limited to a single request at a time per player
The mutex is only held while looking up or creating the bucket; the token accounting itself is done by rate.Limiter, which has its own synchronization
